messages.subject: BSM event tables
parts:
Hi Nick,

It would be nice if you would help me in understanding these event counts. I tried maximum 1000 Maps with number of BSM 200 for 8 ranges. I got following meas tables for dispersal rate. 
This is only means table with some range means:
         A             B            C              D
A     0           47.91       21.39      13.57
B    63.56        0           42.06     39.66
C   48.54      63.72         0          20.64
D  11.74       35.45         7.76       0
what I understand is that it means A-D means dispersal is 13.57 while D-A dispersal means is 11.74. How further we analyse this, like 11.74 time dispersal event occured between D-A? 
would you please add your comments on this or please share if this is clarified in BioGeoBEARS site. 

Thank you!
Best,
Uz

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BSM event tables
parts:
Hi!  I'm not sure I understand the question?

The table has "from" on the left, and "to" on the top.  

So, row A, column D represents the average number of dispersal events from A->D
And row D, column A represents the average number of dispersal events from D->A

Note that even when the range history is, say, ABC -> ABCD (a "d" event, range expansion), the actual dispersal event is modeled as coming from one of the 3 areas (A, B, or C), so the ABC->ABCD event will (1/3 of the time in the simplest case) actually represent a A->D dispersal event.

Other tables give the standard deviation in these event counts, divide up the events (d events versus j events, etc.), etc.

Cheers,
Nick

I wouldn't get mean and standard deviation values for cladogentic events e.g. for vicariance and sympatric process althogh I got total event counts for the two process. 

Thank you!
Best,
UZ
